# bWalletX for Android

The full bWalletX wallet on your Android phone or tablet. Your keys stay on your device.

[Download APK (beta) ↓](https://bwalletx.com/download/bwalletx-android-5.1.83.apk)

It isn't on Google Play yet, so install it by hand:

- Tap Download APK on your Android device.

- If Android asks, allow your browser to install unknown apps (Settings › Apps › your browser › Install unknown apps).

- Open `bwalletx-android-5.1.83.apk` and tap Install.

- Open bWalletX and create or restore your wallet.

Updating from an older version? Install over the top and your wallet stays. If Android says the app can't be updated, write down your 12 words first, then uninstall and reinstall.

Version 5.1.83 beta · 21.0 MB · Android 7+ · SHA-256 7d6fd93395081f42fde0907f67ad47bd89a8909a833f62d0ea779ec567f7ad71

Also: [Chrome extension](https://bwalletx.com/extension) · [Developers](https://bwalletx.com/developers)

# Buy BSV in bWalletX

Open the wallet and the gold Buy BSV card is right at the top, with today’s price. Tap it to buy with a card or bank, or to receive BSV from an exchange or a friend.

Buy BSV$20.26 per BSV

The price on the card is live and updates every minute. You’ll also find the card under the BSV price chart, and a Get BSV button on your BSV row while it’s empty.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

## How it works

### Tap Buy BSV

The gold card at the top of your wallet opens the Get BSV sheet.

### Pick how

Pay with a card, Apple Pay, Google Pay or bank. Or receive from an exchange, another wallet or a friend.

### It lands in your wallet

Your BSV shows up in your wallet, in dollars. Ready to send, mint or trade.

## Ways to get BSV

### From an exchange or another wallet

bWalletX shows your BSV address and QR code. Send from wherever your BSV is now.

### From a friend

Share your $name or paymail. They send to it and it arrives in seconds.

### With a card or bank

Pick a provider in the sheet. It opens in the wallet’s browser. Copy your address from Receive and paste it there.

The card and bank providers in the sheet today:

- Ramp · Apple Pay, Google Pay, card or bank

- BSV Association · buy page run by the BSV Association

- Guardarian · card or bank transfer

- ChangeNOW · card, many currencies

- Alchemy Pay · card, Apple Pay, Google Pay

- Onramper · compares several card providers

- cex.io · card; needs an exchange account

### Good to know

These providers are independent companies, not bWalletX. They check your ID and set their own fees and limits, and what’s on offer depends on where you live. bWalletX never holds your money: you pay the provider, and the BSV goes straight to your own wallet. We’re working on buying with Ramp fully inside the app, with your address filled in for you. It isn’t live yet.

## What can I do with BSV?

### [Mint something](https://bwalletx.com/mint)

Put your art, music or tickets on chain. A photo costs a fraction of a cent.

### [Get PNEEs](https://bwalletx.com/pnees)

Digital cents on BSV, backed by BSV locked in public vaults.

### [Trade on the Exchange](https://bwalletx.com/exchange)

Buy and sell tokens, priced in dollars.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)
[All features](https://bwalletx.com/features)

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# bWalletX for Chrome and Brave

The full bWalletX wallet in Chrome's side panel, and a wallet websites like TokenBlaster can connect to. Your keys stay in the extension.

[Download for Chrome (beta) ↓](https://bwalletx.com/download/bwalletx-extension-5.1.83.zip)
[Download for Brave (beta) ↓](https://bwalletx.com/download/bwalletx-extension-5.1.83.zip)

It isn't on the Chrome Web Store yet, so install it by hand:

- Unzip `bwalletx-extension-5.1.83.zip`.

- Open `chrome://extensions` in Chrome.

- Turn on Developer mode (top right).

- Click Load unpacked and choose the unzipped folder.

- Pin bWalletX, click it, and create or restore your wallet.

## Brave

Same extension, same file. Brave runs Chrome extensions, so:

- Unzip `bwalletx-extension-5.1.83.zip`.

- Open `brave://extensions` in Brave.

- Turn on Developer mode (top right).

- Click Load unpacked and choose the unzipped folder.

- Pin bWalletX from the puzzle-piece menu, click it, and create or restore your wallet.

Version 5.1.83 beta · SHA-256 bd48a6d55335d6ba1576e4b98f647aebcaa8257b24f3d867a4e78026ae2fda7e · Source: [github.com/bitcoin-corp/bwallet](https://github.com/bitcoin-corp/bwallet)

# bWalletX features

One non-custodial BSV wallet for money, names, tokens, rooms, media and apps. Your keys never leave your device.

[Android](https://bwalletx.com/android)
[iPhone · web app](https://bwalletx.com/iphone)
[Chrome extension](https://bwalletx.com/extension)
[Web](https://web.bwalletx.com)

bWalletX only in bWalletX (Android, Chrome, web). Everything else is also in [bWallet](https://www.bwallet.space) from the App Store and Google Play.

## 💰Wallet

### BSV, priced in dollars

Balances and prices in USD; you pay in sats. Live price chart.

### Buy BSV

Buy with a card from inside the wallet, in dollars, sent straight to your address. [How](https://bwalletx.com/buy).

### Send to names

Pay a paymail like `name@bwalletx.com` instead of a long address.

### Tokens and NFTs

Hold, send and receive BSV-21 tokens and 1Sat Ordinals, with a separate ordinals address.

### Pots and standing orders

Set money aside in a pot and pay regular amounts from it. Pause or cancel any time. [How](https://bwalletx.com/subscriptions).

### History and exports

Every transaction for any date range, with a CSV export and a PDF statement. [More](https://bwalletx.com/history).

### Restore from anywhere

12 words are enough. Import from Yours, Panda, RelayX or Twetch, a private key or a backup file.

### Sweep another wallet

Pull funds in from any 12/24-word wallet, scanning its addresses for you.

### Find lost tokens

Recover purchases and tokens that didn't show up, and heal indexing.

### Several accounts

Keep separate accounts, each with its own name.

### bCreditsbWalletX

Top up credits for bCorp apps from the Wallet tab.

## 🪪Names and identity

### Your own paymail

Claim `yourname@bwalletx.com` and receive to it.

### Verified X and Google namesbWalletX

Sign in with X or Google for a verified `name.x` or `name.gmail`, with your photo.

### Every name visible

Settings lists every name your wallet receives at, with one-tap unlink.

### Profile and avatar

An avatar and display name that follow you into chat and the market.

### Signed issuer statements

Every token you mint carries a statement signed by your identity, so anyone can check who made it.

### Verified identity (optional)

An ID check through bit-sign, only when something needs it. [More](https://bwalletx.com/identity#verify).

## ✨Make things

### Your personal tokenbWalletX

Mint a $HANDLE token named after you in one tap. Its icon is your profile picture.

### Mint tokens

Create BSV-21 tokens with your own supply, icon and name.

### Mint NFTs

Inscribe images, music and video as 1Sat Ordinals.

### TicketsbWalletX

Mint a ticket token; sending one invites someone into your room.

## 💬Friends and social

### Token roomsbWalletX

Hold the token, join the room. Every token gets a chat room; its owner sets the rules.

### Friends

Your address book: message, call or pay anyone, and see their token and room.

### Direct messages

Private chats with your contacts.

### Voice and video calls

Call friends straight from the wallet. Turn your camera on or off mid-call and flip between front and back.

### BountiesbWalletX

Post paid tasks in a token room and pay out from your wallet when they're done.

### One feed for BSV social

Twetch, Treechat and bChat posts in one timeline, with full-size images, source badges and bookmarks. Twetch first by default.

### Lock to like

Back a post by time-locking your own BSV against it, plus a most-locked leaderboard.

### Push notifications

DMs always reach you; groups only when you're mentioned, or set each room's bell to All, Mentions or Off. Previews off by default, plus quiet hours. On iPhone, Android, the web and Chrome. [More](https://bwalletx.com/push).

### $b in every room

Type `/b` in any chat and bWalletX's own assistant answers there, day or night. `/b` on its own lists the commands.

### bWallet Lounge

The community room on [bChat](https://www.bitcoinchat.online/room/LOUNGE): ask questions, meet other users, talk to the team.

## 📈Exchange and media

### The exchangebWalletX

Buy and sell tokens and NFTs wallet to wallet, including every $HANDLE token and verified X accounts.

### Browse the market

Explore tokens and NFTs, filtered for safety.

### SellbWalletX

List your tokens and NFTs at your own price from the wallet.

### Safety filter

Always-on filter for unsafe content in the market; your own items blur instead.

### Media player

Play music and video ordinals you own, with a mini player.

### SharesbWalletX

See company share listings in the market.

## 🧩Apps and websites

### bApps store

A built-in store of Bitcoin apps, one tap away. Desktop- or phone-sized.

### Browser

Open BSV apps inside the wallet; they can ask it to pay or sign.

### Connect to websites

A BRC-100 wallet sites can connect to. [For developers](https://bwalletx.com/developers).

### Pair by QR

Scan a site's QR with your phone to connect it, and see or remove paired sites.

### b agent

A help assistant with your own AI key, or pay per message from the wallet.

## 👻Agents

### Agent accountsbWalletX

Give an AI its own account with a budget and a daily cap. Each one gets a little pixel ghost in its own colour, on the card and as its avatar. [How it works](https://bwalletx.com/agent).

### Stop allbWalletX

One tap freezes every agent; a stopped agent can't spend. Every action is logged in dollars.

### bAgentsbWalletX

The ghost house: see all your agents, their balances and spending today, and stop or resume them. At [agents.bwalletx.com](https://agents.bwalletx.com).

### CLI and MCP

Pair a computer or Claude to an agent account with `npx bwalletx`. [CLI](https://bwalletx.com/cli) · [MCP](https://bwalletx.com/mcp).

## 🔐Security

### Non-custodial

Keys are created and stored on your device. We never see them.

### Approve every request

Nothing is signed or paid without your tap; set a one-tap limit for small payments.

### Face ID and fingerprint

Unlock with biometrics on your phone.

### Strong passwords

Generate a strong password and change it anytime.

### Delete your account

Remove your paymail, profile and messages from our servers whenever you like.

Some features are still in beta and vary by platform. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# History. Where your money went.

Every transaction your account has made, read from the chain. Pick a date range, see what came in and went out, and export it in a form your accountant can use.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

## What it does today

- LiveFull on-chain history. Every transaction that touched the account’s addresses, not just ones made on this device.

- LiveDate ranges. 7 days, 30 days, this year, all time, or your own dates.

- LiveSummary. In, out, fees and net for the range.

- LiveLabels. Tips, likes, pot payments and agent spend are named where the wallet can tell.

- LiveCSV export. A spreadsheet of the range, one row per transaction.

- LivePDF statement. A printable statement of the range. On a phone, open it and use Print › Save as PDF.

- LiveTokens and NFTs. Buys, sells, listings, cancels, transfers and mints, each showing the token or NFT and the amount. Since 5.1.82.

- LiveGames, subscriptions and apps. Payments to games, pots and subscriptions, and apps you connected, each with its own label. Since 5.1.82.

- LiveCategory filters. All, Payments, Tokens, NFTs, Games, Subscriptions, Apps, Social. Exports include the category, asset and app. Since 5.1.82.

- LiveConnections log. Which apps used the wallet, when, what you allowed them, what each spent, and a button to revoke access. Recorded on each device from 5.1.82.

- LiveGains and losses. A Gains tab with realised gains and losses per tax year: UK HMRC share-pooling rules in pounds by default, FIFO in dollars elsewhere, BSV tracked as an asset, and a disposals CSV for your accountant. Since 5.1.83. Gains is in beta: figures may be incomplete, so check them against your own records.

Open it from the wallet: tap History on the account card. Payments from a pot show there too; see [Subscriptions and Pots](https://bwalletx.com/subscriptions).

History and its exports are records, not tax advice. Check with an accountant before you file.

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# bWalletX on iPhone

Apple only allows App Store apps on iPhone, and the App Store edition (bWallet) can’t trade. Until there’s a better route, bWalletX on iPhone is a web app: the full wallet, installed from Safari onto your Home Screen. Read [where your keys are](#keys) before you use it.

Open in Safari→Share→Add to Home Screen

## Install it (one minute)

- On your iPhone, open [web.bwalletx.com](https://web.bwalletx.com) in Safari.

- Tap the Share button (the square with an arrow).

- Scroll down and tap Add to Home Screen, then Add.

- Open bWalletX from your Home Screen, and create or restore your wallet there.

## Where your keys are, honestly

### On your phone, not on our servers

The web app is the same non-custodial wallet: your keys are created on the phone, encrypted with your password, and kept in the app’s own storage on the device. We never see them.

### But web storage is more fragile than a real app

iPhone can clear a website’s storage. The installed Home Screen app is much safer than a Safari tab: it has its own storage, the app asks iOS to keep it, and the “7 days unused” rule only counts days you open it. It can still be lost if you delete the Home Screen icon, clear website data in Settings, or don’t open it for a long time. A Safari tab is cleared much sooner, so always use the icon.

### So: it makes you back up first

Before you can receive money, the web app makes you back up. Either save an encrypted backup file (locked with your wallet password) to Files or email it to yourself, or write down your recovery phrase on paper and confirm three of the words. Keep the password with the file; with either backup you can restore the wallet in any bWallet or bWalletX, on any device. Every month it checks you still have it.

It’s still a beta: keep small amounts in it.

## What’s different from Android

### The same wallet

Tokens, the Exchange and Strategies, names, chat rooms, agent accounts and the b agent all work, and the same recovery phrase works in every edition.

### A few phone features are limited

No Face ID unlock: you use your password. Pairing the [CLI](https://bwalletx.com/cli) works while the app is open on screen.

## Prefer the App Store?

bWallet is our App Store edition: send, receive, tokens, names and rooms. It has no Market or Exchange; trading is only in bWalletX. It hasn’t been submitted to the App Store yet: that waits on converting our Apple developer account to an organisation account. [Join the waitlist](https://www.bwallet.space/#waitlist) to hear when it’s out.

[Open web.bwalletx.com](https://web.bwalletx.com)
[Other devices](https://bwalletx.com/get)

# Push notifications

Never miss a message. Push notifications are live since version 5.1.70 and reach you even with the app closed: on your phone, the web wallet and the Chrome extension. They run through our own push server, push.bwalletx.com.

LiveiPhoneAndroidWebChrome extension

## Where it works

### iPhone

Apple Push Notifications.

### Android

Firebase Cloud Messaging.

### Web wallet and Chrome extension

Web Push, so your browser can tell you even when the tab isn't open.

## Turning it on

Go to Settings › Notifications › Push notifications. In the phone apps the switch starts on. In the web wallet and the Chrome extension it starts off: turn it on there and your browser asks for permission. The switch is per device; previews and quiet hours belong to your account and follow you to every device.

## What notifies you

- Direct messages from friends, always.

- Group chats: each group has a bell with All, Mentions or Off. Groups start on Mentions, so busy rooms don't buzz you all day.

- Mentions of your `$name`.

- Photos, voice and video messages sent to a room you're in.

- $b answers to your `/b` questions.

- Requests to sign or witness a document.

Tapping a notification opens the room or screen it's about. Several messages in quick succession are collapsed into one.

## Privacy

By default a notification says who messaged you, not what they wrote, so nothing private shows on your lock screen. If you want message previews, turn on Show message previews. Quiet hours silence notifications overnight or whenever you choose. No message text is stored on our push server.

You can turn notifications off per group with the bell, or entirely in Settings › Notifications. Your keys never leave your device; notifications don't need them.

## bWalletX and bWallet

Notifications work the same in both editions: bWalletX here, and bWallet, the App Store and Google Play version.

[Social in bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/social)

# Restore. Bring your coins home.

Have an old BSV wallet? Its 12 words still work. bWalletX can open it as an account, or move what’s in it into one of yours.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

## Restore or sweep?

Restore opens the old wallet as an account in bWalletX. The keys are the same, so nothing moves on chain. Use it when bWalletX knows the wallet’s layout.

Sweep moves the coins and tokens out of the old wallet into an account you already have, in new transactions. Use it for wallets that spread coins across many addresses, or when you just want everything in one place. Sweeping pays a small network fee.

## Wallets you can bring in

WalletHowYou needDerivation pathWhat comes across

bWalletX, Yours, Panda
LiveRestore as an account12 words`m/44'/236'/0'/1/0` payment
`m/44'/236'/1'/0/0` ordinals
`m/0'/236'/0'/0/0` identityEverything: BSV, ordinals, BSV-20 and BSV-21 tokens, names. Coins on Yours' older payment key (`m/44'/236'/0'/0/0`) are moved across automatically.

RelayX
LiveRestore as an account12 words`m/44'/236'/0'/0/0` payment
`m/44'/236'/0'/2/0` ordinalsEverything on those two keys.

Twetch
LiveRestore as an account12 words`m/0/0` paymentEverything on that key.

SimplyCash
LiveNew wallet, then sweep12 words, or SimplyCash’s recovery string (words:path:passphrase)`m/44'/145'/0'`, receive and change chains, gap limit 20. Early SimplyCash wallets’ older derivation is tried too.BSV, ordinals, BSV-21 tokens. SimplyCash spreads coins over many addresses, so it can’t be one account; it is swept instead.

Other BIP44 wallets

Money Button
LiveSweep into an account12 words, passphrase if it had one`m/44'/0'/0'`, receive chainBSV and anything else on those addresses. Money Button tokens (SFP) are found, listed and left where they are.

## What stays behind, and why

- Names, BSV-20 tokens and locked coins are not swept. The sweep screen tells you how many it found. Restore the wallet as an account instead to keep them.

- Money Button tokens (SFP). Each one can only be spent with a signature from Money Button’s token server, which shut down with Money Button in 2022. Nobody can move or burn them alone. bWalletX keeps them out of the BSV sweep so they are not destroyed by accident, and lists them for you.

- HandCash, Centbee, ElectrumSV and others aren’t listed by name. If you have their 12 or 24 words, try a sweep: bWalletX tries every path above. If it finds nothing, tell us.

## How to restore

- On the welcome screen, choose to restore a wallet.

- Pick the wallet: bWalletX (also Yours and Panda), RelayX, Twetch, SimplyCash (phone app), Restore with private key, Restore from master backup, or Other.

- Type your words (or key) and set a password. For Other, turn on Use custom derivations to enter your own paths.

## How to sweep

- Open Settings › Account data › Sweep into this account.

- Paste the recovery phrase, private key (WIF) or xprv. Add the passphrase only if the old wallet had one, and a custom path if you know it.

- bWalletX scans every known layout and shows what it found. Check it, then sweep. You get a link to each transaction.

## Stay safe

- Never type your words into a website, a chat or a form. Only into the wallet app itself.

- bWalletX derives every key on your device. Your words are never sent anywhere and are not stored after a sweep.

- A sweep moves funds in new transactions. Once they’re in, the old words no longer hold anything you swept.

## Don’t see your wallet?

[Tell us](mailto:support@bwalletx.com?subject=Restore%20from%20another%20wallet) which one, and we’ll look at adding it.

The story behind this page: [022 Bring your coins home](https://bwalletx.com/blog/022-bring-your-coins-home).

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Handles. Your name is your paymail.

There is no account ID and no email needed: your 12 words are the account. On top of them you get a $handle people can pay and message, and it can be your token and your room too.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

Need to prove who you are in the real world, privately? See [Identity](https://bwalletx.com/identity).

## $handles

- Live$handles. A name people can pay and message, which is also your paymail.

- LiveNumbered handles. New accounts get a free numbered handle, from $bwallet0101 onward. $bwallet0001 to 0100 are reserved.

- LiveRenames. Change to a name you prove you hold. Your rooms and messages move with you.

- LiveYour token and your room. In bWalletX your $handle can be a personal token, with a room named after you. See [Features](https://bwalletx.com/features).

- ComingMore than one handle per account. The groundwork is in; adding a second handle is not.

- ComingHandle NFTs. Own your handle as an NFT you can hold or sell, separate from your account.

## Linked accounts ($401)

Link other accounts to your on-chain identity. Each link adds to your identity strength, so others can see more than one source vouches for you.

- LiveIn the wallet: X and Google, under Settings › Identity.

- LiveOn bit-sign: X, Google, GitHub, Discord and LinkedIn.

## Card signature

- LiveYour signature on your card. Draw it once. It shows on the back of your wallet card. It stays on your device and is not put on chain.

Signing documents and contracts is on [/sign](https://bwalletx.com/sign).

- LiveSign in with bWalletX. Apps can let you sign in with your wallet instead of a password. Your wallet signs a one-time challenge; no password or email is shared. For developers: [/connect](https://bwalletx.com/connect).

# Identity. Verified when you need it. Private when you don’t.

Your wallet doesn’t need your name. Some things do. When one of them comes up, you verify once, and your wallet can then show that a real person stands behind it without carrying your details around.

Looking for names, $handles and sign-in? They’re on [Handles](https://bwalletx.com/handles).

## Why some things need a real identity

Most of the wallet works with no name at all. A few things are different, because the other side has to know who they are dealing with:

- Signing a contract that has to bind a real person.

- Investing in a private placement.

- Services that are regulated and must know their customer.

You are only asked when something needs it.

## Verify once

The check is run by Veriff, through bit-sign. You show an ID document and take a selfie in Veriff’s flow. When Veriff approves, bit-sign records the result and your wallet can fetch a certificate that says you are verified.

- LiveID check with Veriff, through bit-sign.

- LiveCertificate in your wallet. Your wallet proves it owns its key, and bit-sign issues a certificate to that key.

## Who sees what

- VeriffYour document and selfie. Veriff handles them in its own flow.

- bit-signThe result. bit-sign keeps your name, date of birth and document type, and checks your name against sanctions lists.

- Your walletA certificate with no name and no date of birth. It says you are verified, whether you are over 18, the country of your document, the check level and its dates. Each of those is encrypted, so the wallet can show one without the others.

- On chainNothing personal. Your name, date of birth and documents are not put on chain.

### Who can see the result, and when

- In a bit-sign deal room, a host can ask a named member for a check. The member chooses to accept. The room then sees that the check was submitted, and whether it was approved or declined. It does not see your name, date of birth or documents.

- bit-sign’s signed record of your check is private. Only you, signed in, can see all of it: the check level, the type and country of your document, the sanctions result and the date. It has no name and no date of birth. Anyone else who looks it up with your key gets “not found”, the same answer as for a key with no check, so they can’t even tell you’ve been checked.

- Sharing part of it with one person is your choice: you sign a grant naming the fields, the person’s key and an end date, and they see only those fields until then. The same goes for an issuer asking bit-sign whether you meet its rules: without your grant it gets “not found”, and with one it sees only the checks your grant covers. The sanctions result is shown to them only as pass or fail, and never to the public.

## Using it

- LiveSign and seal. Sign .NDS.HTML contracts on bit-sign with your drawn signature and your wallet key in one step, sealed on chain, from the Chrome extension or a paired phone. Only hashes go on chain, never the document. If a paid seal is interrupted, it can be recovered rather than paid twice. More: [/sign](https://bwalletx.com/sign).

- LiveChecks in deal rooms. A counterparty sees approved or declined, not your documents.

- ComingShowing one fact from your wallet. The certificate is built so the wallet can reveal a single field, such as over 18, to an app. A finished flow for that is still being built.

- ComingThe rest of the investor journey. One-tap pay from the wallet and a single investor flow are still being built.

## Deleting your data

- LiveDelete account in the wallet’s Settings removes your bit-sign account, handle, linked accounts and chats. The records of an identity check are kept, because anti-money-laundering rules require identity checks to be kept for a period.

- ComingSelf-serve deletion of your check. Not built yet. Until it is, ask [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com).

- NoteAnything on chain cannot be deleted by anyone. That is why nothing personal is put there.

## Keys

Your keys are made and kept on your device. They are not sent to us. Lose your 12 words and nobody, including us, can recover the account.

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

Source: https://bwalletx.com/lock

# Lock. Even you can’t unlock it early.

Lock BSV on the Bitcoin SV blockchain until a date you choose, or have it paid back to you a little at a time. Once it’s locked, nobody can move it before then: not you, not bWalletX, not anyone.

Live since 5.1.84 Lock BSV is in the app: tap the lock in the top bar. It is a new feature, so start small. Lock only small amounts, a few thousand satoshis, until it has been out for a while. The app asks again if you try to lock more than 0.01 BSV.

## What locking is

A lock is a normal BSV output with a small contract attached. The contract says two things: these coins can only be spent by your key, and only in a transaction that the network won’t accept before a certain block height. Blocks come about every ten minutes, so a height is a date, roughly.

The rule is enforced by every miner, not by us. There is no switch at bWalletX that releases a lock early, and no support process that can. The coins never leave your wallet’s keys; they just can’t move until the height is reached.

## Two kinds of lock

- One unlock date. The whole amount opens at one block height.

- Gradual payouts. The amount is split into pieces, each locked to a later height: daily, weekly, monthly or every few days, for a number of payouts or until an end date. You choose how each payout is sized:

• Dollars per payout (the default), for example $10 a day. You lock BSV, sized at today’s price plus a buffer (20% unless you change it). When a piece unlocks, your wallet pays out the dollar amount at that day’s price. If the piece is worth more, it offers to re-lock the extra into the next payout; if it is worth less, you get the whole piece and the schedule shows what it came to, for example “paid $8.40 of $10”. If the wallet can’t get a current price, it doesn’t guess: the piece stays in your wallet as BSV.

• BSV per payout, for example 0.1 BSV a week.

• A percentage, of the original amount (the same payout each time, ending after 100÷X payouts) or of what is left (shrinking payouts; the last small remainder is paid at once).

Before you lock, the wallet shows every payout: estimated date, block height, BSV, and estimated dollars at today’s price.

## Read this before you lock

- It is irreversible. You type LOCK to confirm. After that, nobody can unlock it early, including you and bWalletX.

- It is BSV. The locked asset is BSV, and its dollar value goes up and down while it is locked. Dollar amounts are targets, not guarantees. The price is only used inside your own wallet, at payout time.

- Dates are approximate. A lock opens at a block height. If blocks come faster or slower than ten minutes on average, the day moves.

- Your 12 words are the only key. Lose them and the locks are lost for good. Nobody can recover them.

- Limits. Each payout must be at least 1,000 sats, because claiming one costs a small fee. One lock holds up to 520 payouts; longer percentage schedules keep the later payouts in one lock and re-split it when it opens.

## Claiming

When a lock opens, the Locks screen shows it as Ready to claim. One tap claims every opened piece, across all your locks, back into your wallet in a single transaction.

## A public receipt, if you want one

Some people lock coins to show others they can’t sell them: a founder vesting their own coins, a creator showing they aren’t about to cash out. For that, you can turn on Mint a public receipt. It is off by default.

The receipt is an NFT made in the same transaction as the locks. It shows the amount, the schedule and who locked it (your handle, if you have one), and says “Verify at bwalletx.com/lock/verify”. A picture proves nothing by itself, so the check reads the transaction from the chain and confirms that its outputs really are locks with those heights and amounts, and whether they have been claimed yet.

Turning it on links your identity to the amount, publicly and permanently. Only do it if you mean to.

[Verify a lock](https://bwalletx.com/lock/verify)

Why we built it: [023 Locks you can’t break](https://bwalletx.com/blog/023-lock-bsv).

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Nothing here is investment advice. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

---

Source: https://bwalletx.com/lock/verify

# Verify a lock.

Paste the transaction id of a lock or lock receipt. This page reads it from the chain (WhatsOnChain) and checks every lock output itself. It doesn’t trust the receipt’s picture.

Check

## What is checked

- Each output that is a lock: its unlock height and amount, read from the script the network enforces.

- If the transaction has a bWalletX receipt: that every payout it lists matches a real lock output, to the same key, with the same height and amount, and that the totals add up.

- Whether each lock has been spent (claimed), from WhatsOnChain. Status: Locked, Partly claimed or Fully claimed.

Heights are block numbers; dates are about 144 blocks a day. [About Lock BSV](https://bwalletx.com/lock).

Source: https://bwalletx.com/mint

# Make something. Mint it.

Minting puts your thing on Bitcoin SV. After that it’s yours: you can sell it, send it to a friend, or let people collect it. All from the Mint button in bWalletX.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

## What you can make

### Art & photos

One of a kind, or a numbered collection.

A painting you photographed, sold as a single piece. Or 50 numbered prints of your best shot.

Straight from the Mint button.

### Music

Tracks fans own and play in their wallet.

Release a single as 100 copies. Fans keep it, play it, and can pass it on.

Straight from the Mint button.

### Videos & films

Clips, shorts or a whole film.

A short film, a behind-the-scenes clip, or episode one of your series.

Straight from the Mint button. Up to 10 MB per file.

### Books & PDFs

Ebooks, zines, guides, reports.

A zine, a recipe book, or a guide you wrote, as a PDF, ebook or text file.

Straight from the Mint button.

### A website

A one-page site, on chain for good.

A one-page portfolio, a wedding page, or a manifesto that nobody can take down.

Straight from the Mint button, as one HTML page.

### Tickets & passes

Entry to your chatroom, event or site.

Sell 30 passes to your private chatroom, or tickets to a gig. Holding one lets you in.

Straight from the Mint button.

### A coin or memecoin

Your own token, fixed supply.

A coin for your club, your community or just for fun. You pick the name and how many exist.

Straight from the Mint button.

### Contracts

Agreements both sides sign.

A deal with a client: half up front, half when the work is delivered.

b, the wallet’s AI assistant, drafts it with you.

### Trading strategies

Package a strategy others can buy.

A rule like “buy this token weekly, stop at $50”, packaged so others can buy and run it.

b, the wallet’s AI assistant, drafts it with you.

### An app

List your bApp with its own token.

You built an app. List it in the wallet’s Apps tab with a token of its own.

b, the wallet’s AI assistant, drafts it with you.

## What it costs

### Usually well under a cent for a photo

You pay the Bitcoin SV network to store your file, so the price depends on its size. A typical photo costs a fraction of a cent. A 1 MB file is about two cents. A full 10 MB video is about 20 cents. bWalletX adds a 1% fee on top of the network fee. Starting a new collection takes one extra transaction, so it roughly doubles the cost of that first mint.

The wallet shows the exact price in dollars before you confirm. Prices here assume BSV at about $20 and the wallet’s standard network fee; they move with the BSV price. The limit is 10 MB per file; the wallet can shrink a big photo for you.

## Contracts and new kinds of instruments

A contract in bWalletX is an agreement that both sides sign. Once it is locked on chain, it pays out by its own rules: money goes where the contract says, when the contract says. b, the wallet’s AI assistant, helps you draft it. It asks who it’s between, what each side agrees to, the price and the dates.

### Please read this

Anything that works like an investment, such as shares, bonds or a pension, may be regulated where you live. You are responsible for following the law. bWalletX is a wallet: it does not offer investments, and it can’t tell you whether something you make is allowed. If in doubt, ask a lawyer before you mint or sell it.

## Questions

### Is it permanent?

Yes. Inscriptions on Bitcoin SV can’t be deleted. So don’t mint anything you don’t own, and nothing illegal.

### Who owns it?

Whoever holds it in their wallet. When you mint, that’s you. Your keys stay on your device; we can’t move your things.

### Can I sell it?

Yes. List it on the [Exchange](https://bwalletx.com/exchange) tab, set a price in dollars, and buyers pay in BSV. You can also just send it to someone.

### Does it work on my phone and in Chrome?

Yes. bWalletX runs on [Android](https://bwalletx.com/android), [iPhone](https://bwalletx.com/iphone) and as a [Chrome extension](https://bwalletx.com/extension). Contracts, strategies and apps need the full bWalletX (with b, the assistant).

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)
[All features](https://bwalletx.com/features)

# PNEEs · Penny Stablecoins

Digital pennies on BSV. Each PNEE is one US cent (ticker $PNEE), backed only by BSV locked in public vaults. Notes are cash: spend them, send them, price things in them. No bank account behind them, no co-signer on your transfers, nobody who can freeze them.

Lock BSV→Mint PNEEs→Spend them

## How it works

### Notes are pennies that add up

One PNEE unit is one cent. A $10 note is just 1,000 of them together; they split and combine like any token, and the wallet shows dollars. PNEE is an ordinary BSV-21 token, so any 1Sat-compatible wallet can hold it.

### Vaults: lock BSV, mint notes

Anyone can lock BSV in a vault contract and mint notes against it, up to a tenth of its value to start (10x collateral). They keep their BSV and its upside; to unlock it, they hand the notes back. BSV went from $11 to $20 in three months, so we started very safe: a vault survives an 85% fall in BSV.

### Liquidation keeps every note backed

If BSV falls so far that a vault drops below 150%, anyone may repay its notes and take its BSV at a 10% discount. The price comes from 3 of 5 signers, using the median, with fresh timestamps.

### No interest

Notes are cash, like banknotes: holders don’t earn interest and vault owners don’t pay a yearly fee. The vault owner’s reward is spendable dollars without selling their BSV.

## PNEEs and MNEE

PNEEsMNEE

Backed byBSV locked in public vaults, visible on chainUS dollars held by a company

Can your transfer be blocked?No: notes move freelyEvery transfer is co-signed by MNEE’s server

If BSV crashesProtected by 10x collateral and liquidationsUnaffected (dollar reserves)

## The mainnet pilot (live)

PNEEs are live on BSV mainnet in a small, capped pilot: a $5 cap per vault and $10 in total.

- Token: [1599c4e49a…_0](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/1599c4e49a28c7791295f50613e1545aa9246dd592ae8b8f696b81916a475ae4) (BSV-21, 2 decimals). The whole supply sits in the issuer treasury; notes leave it only when a vault mints.

- First vault: [3a782a53…](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/3a782a53ea17fdea202488c7d4e0ca335be85d1663b9a6bfb87e9435245d78f2), 12,500,000 sats of BSV (about $2.54) locked.

- First mint: [de18356c…](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/de18356cb0560547d68776941a921c28fe04227b7f9e892ebbefbd1e43a00980), 25 PNEEs, checked against a 3-of-5 price of $20.32.

- First release: [913e2a78…](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/913e2a786da02d21b86d4d688e25a3879879ac6e62130cfd0ebacb4657145c5a), 25 PNEE from the treasury to the vault owner.

- First liquidation (5 Oct 2026): a small, clearly labelled demo vault ([9f9f5343…](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/9f9f53438a8a2463935eadf62bc221f4d035c9e1c55e0376fad801ed6de4a727), 1,000,000 sats, 2 PNEEs) whose on-chain rules allow liquidation below 1100%, so it could be shown at the real price. At a 3-of-5 median of $20.09 the vault stood at 1000%. The liquidator burned the 2 PNEEs ([640acc97…](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/640acc972dd08f95b027d4ddc58bf39ce1c45782c73d15300b92f590dd4e0d29)) and liquidated the vault ([7d496a59…](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/7d496a59ef82e3dfbb763f52cae5063535c4273a9812ac643714da093400be4e)): the contract paid the liquidator the debt plus the 10% discount (106,558 sats after the fee) and returned the rest, 890,493 sats, to the vault owner. Real vaults use 150%; the main pilot vault is at about 1000% and is not liquidatable.

## What we haven’t solved yet

### Honest trust model

The vault contract can’t yet see by itself that notes were really burned, so for now the issuer (bCorp) co-signs note releases and burns, in public on chain. The five price signers are run by us during the pilot. Both are fine for a few dollars and not for real money: independent price signers and an on-chain burn check come before any meaningful amount.

[Exchange › Bonds](https://bwalletx.com/exchange)

PNEEs are an experiment. Don’t put in more than you can lose. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Pots. Set money aside. Pay from it.

A pot is money you set aside inside your wallet. Regular payments come out of it, and never more than is in it. Stop it any time, without asking anyone.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

## What a pot is

A pot is a named account inside your wallet, like Rent or Savings. It has its own balance. You fill it from your main account and top it up whenever you like.

Each pot has a Top up option, a Stop this pot switch, and its own History of every payment, with a link to each transaction on chain.

## The most you can lose

The pot balance is the most any payment from it can ever take. If a pot is empty, nothing more can leave it. Your main account is never touched by a pot payment.

## Paying from a pot

Standing orders pay a person or a paymail a fixed dollar amount, daily, weekly or monthly, from a pot. Subscriptions are the same thing paid to an app or service. Both are covered on the [Subscriptions](https://bwalletx.com/subscriptions) page.

Payments go out when you open the app on or after each date. If you miss a few dates, the next open catches up, up to three payments; more than that, it asks you first. If notifications are on, the wallet tells you when a pot is running low or a payment fails.

## Pause, resume, stop

Open Settings › Subscriptions and tap a pot. Each payment card has Pause, Resume and Cancel. To stop everything in a pot at once, use Stop this pot; resume it the same way.

## What works today

- LivePots. Name, fund, top up, stop and resume. Each has its own balance and history.

- LivePayments from pots. Standing orders and subscriptions, capped by the pot balance.

- LiveLow-balance and failed-payment reminders.

- ComingPayments while the app is closed. Future payments signed in advance (nLockTime), so the payee can collect each on its date.

- ComingPots in PNEEs. Pots that hold and pay penny tokens, so a 1¢ payment stays 1¢.

## bWallet (App Store and Google Play) and bWalletX

- LiveBoth: pots, standing orders to a person or paymail, pause, resume, stop and reminders. Pots are free.

- LivebWalletX only: subscriptions to apps and services paid from a pot. Store rules don’t allow these in the store edition.

Why we are building this: [016 Pots](https://bwalletx.com/blog/016-pots).

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

Source: https://bwalletx.com/sign

# Your signature

Your wallet card has a signature strip on the back, like a bank card. In bWalletX 5.1.77 you can sign it with your finger. You can now also sign contracts on bit-sign with bWalletX and seal them on Bitcoin.

Flip the card→
Sign with your finger→
Save

## Sign your card

- On the Wallet tab, tap your card to flip it over.

- On the back, under AUTHORISED SIGNATURE, tap the pen. Pressing and holding the strip works too.

- A full-screen pad opens. Sign with your finger, or with a mouse in the Chrome extension. With the phone upright, the pad turns so you sign along the length of the phone and get more room.

- Use Undo to take back the last stroke or Clear to start again, then tap Save.

Your signature now shows on the back of the card. To change it, tap the pen again and choose Redraw signature or Remove signature.

The card also turns more golden as your balance grows.

## Where it's kept

### On your device only

The signature is stored on the phone or computer you drew it on. It isn't sent to a server and it isn't put on-chain. bApps and websites can't read it.

### One per account

Each account in your wallet has its own signature. If you have a personal and a business account, sign each one separately.

### Ready for contracts

It's saved in a fixed format (one SVG path in a 1000 × 250 box) with a SHA-256 fingerprint, so the same drawing always gives the same fingerprint. That's what lets it be signed and checked later.

The signature isn't in your 12-word recovery phrase. If you restore your wallet on a new phone, sign again.

## Sign and seal contracts New

bit-sign contracts (`.nds.html` files) have signature boxes. With Sign and seal with bWalletX on [bit-sign](https://www.bit-sign.online), you:

- draw your signature into your box in the contract;

- approve in bWalletX, which signs a record of what you signed with your wallet's identity key;

- approve the seal on Bitcoin. That costs the network fee only, under a penny. bit-sign charges nothing.

Today that takes two approvals in your wallet: one to sign, one to pay. Nothing is sent until you approve. If anything interrupts after you've paid, reopen the document and bit-sign finishes the seal for you, for up to 24 hours. You never pay twice.

Coming next: one tap. bWalletX will hand over the signature from your card and show its own screen with the document title, the box you're signing, your signature and the cost, then sign and pay together.

Only fingerprints (hashes) go on-chain, never the document or your signature. Your contract stays private between the people signing it.

### Anyone can check it

Anyone with a copy of the sealed contract can confirm three things: its fingerprint is on-chain, the identity key's signature is valid, and the drawn signature hasn't been changed since.

### Works where you are

On a computer, through the bWalletX Chrome extension. Or pair your phone by scanning a QR code and approve there, for a contract open on your computer.

This gives you an electronic signature backed by strong evidence of who signed, what and when. Whether a particular document can be signed electronically depends on the document and the law where you are; some documents, such as wills and deeds that need a witness, can't. This page isn't legal advice.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)
[All features](https://bwalletx.com/features)
[Chrome extension](https://bwalletx.com/extension)
[Privacy](https://bwalletx.com/privacy)

The card signature is in bWalletX 5.1.77 and later (Android APK, Chrome extension, web and iPhone) and in bWallet, the App Store and Google Play version. Sign and seal is live on bit-sign for bWalletX users (Chrome extension or a paired phone). Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Subscriptions. Set it, cap it, stop it.

Put money aside in a pot. Set up regular payments from it. The pot balance is the most they can ever take. Pause or cancel any time, without asking anyone.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

## Paid from pots

Every subscription and standing order pays from a pot: money you set aside, whose balance is the most it can ever take. How pots work: [Pots](https://bwalletx.com/pots).

## Standing orders and subscriptions

A standing order pays a person or a paymail a fixed dollar amount: daily, weekly or monthly. You choose the first payment date and, if you like, how many payments to make.

A subscription is the same thing paid to an app or service. Today that means our own services, bChat and the $b agent, and only in bWalletX.

Payments go out when you open the app on or after each date. If notifications are on, the wallet reminds you the day before, and tells you when a pot is running low or a payment fails. If you miss a few dates, the next open catches up, up to three payments; more than that, it asks you first.

## What works today

- LivePots. Name, fund, top up, stop and resume. Each has its own balance and history.

- LiveStanding orders. To a person or paymail, daily, weekly or monthly, from a pot.

- LiveSubscriptions to our services. bChat and the $b agent, in bWalletX only.

- LivePause, resume, cancel. One tap on each payment card.

- LiveReminders. A notice the day before a payment, when a pot runs low, and when a payment fails.

- ComingPayments while the app is closed. Signing future payments in advance (nLockTime), so the payee can collect each one on its date. Pausing would cancel the unsent ones.

- ComingSubscribe with bWalletX. A way for any app or site to ask your wallet for a subscription.

- ComingPaying in PNEEs. Pots that hold and pay penny tokens, so a 1¢ payment stays 1¢.

## Set one up

- Open Settings and tap Subscriptions.

- Create a pot and give it a name.

- Fund it from your main account.

- Add a payment: who to pay, the amount in dollars, how often, the first date and, optionally, how many payments.

## See and cancel them

Open Settings › Subscriptions and tap a pot. Each payment has a card showing who it pays, how much, and the next date. Tap Pause to hold it, Resume to restart it, or Cancel to end it. To stop everything in a pot at once, use Stop this pot.

Every payment shows in the pot’s History. In the wallet’s [History](https://bwalletx.com/history) screen, payments from a pot are labelled “pot payment”.

## The 1¢ a day idea

One idea is that unlocking subscriptions to apps and services costs 1¢ a day, paid from a pot like anything else. That is not switched on. Nobody is charged for it today, and it would never be on in the App Store or Google Play edition. Pots and standing orders stay free.

## bWallet (App Store and Google Play) and bWalletX

- LiveBoth: pots, standing orders to a person or paymail, pause, resume, cancel and reminders.

- LivebWalletX only: subscriptions to apps and services, and any future 1¢-a-day option. Store rules don’t allow these in the store edition.

Why we are building this: [016 Pots](https://bwalletx.com/blog/016-pots).

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Coordinate on BSV. Talk where the money is.

BSV is a messaging protocol at heart. Every transaction can carry a message. So the conversation about BSV should live on BSV, in the same wallet that holds your coins and tokens.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)[Open bChat](https://www.bitcoinchat.online)

## Why

Twitter, Reddit and Telegram put every community in one room, and BSV threads there get buried or piled on. We still post there, because that is where new people are. But the planning should happen on BSV, where every account is a wallet and, as paid messages arrive, spam costs money. Advertise there, coordinate here. The full argument: [021 Coordinate on BSV](https://bwalletx.com/blog/021-coordinate-on-bsv).

## Chat in your wallet

Chat is part of bWalletX. You don’t sign up anywhere else: your wallet is your account, and the people you talk to can pay you, and you them, in the same place. bChat is the full version, on the web and inside the wallet.

Other BSV networks are already here, and Chat reads from them rather than replacing them:

[### Twetch
One of the longest-running BSV social apps.](https://twetch.com)
[### Treechat
Threaded posts and replies on BSV.](https://app.treechat.com)
[### Fwetch
Boards on the Vulpine network.](https://fwetch.lol)
[### Peck
A BSV feed built on Bitcoin Schema.](https://peck.to)
[### bChat
Our full chat app. Rooms, feed and messages.](https://www.bitcoinchat.online)

Twetch, Treechat, Fwetch and Peck are made by other teams, not The Bitcoin Corporation.

## What Chat does

Each item is marked by what the code does today.

- LiveMessage boards. Open rooms in bChat: public or invite-only, anyone signed in can start one. The bChat feed also reads Twetch, Treechat, Fwetch and Peck posts in one place.

- LiveToken-gated rooms. Hold a BSV-21 token or 1Sat collection and its room appears in your Chat list. Sell it and the room goes. bChat checks the holding on every read and post. Not in bWallet, the App Store and Google Play edition.

- LivePrivate messages. Direct messages between wallets, with blocking and reporting.

- LiveVoice and video calls. One-to-one calls between friends. Either side can turn the camera on or off during a call.

- LiveTips. Tip the author of a post in BSV, paid to their own verified address.

- ComingOne-to-many video streams. Broadcast to a room. Not built yet.

- ComingPay per message. Rooms already have a price-per-message setting. Charging it is not switched on yet.

- ComingPay per second. Pay for a call or stream by the second while it runs.

- ComingPay with tokens. Pay for messages and calls in a token instead of BSV.

- ComingSet your price to be reached. Choose what strangers pay to message or call you. Friends stay free.

## Start now

Download bWalletX, open the Chat tab, and join the bWallet Lounge. Buy a token to get into its room. Or open bChat in a browser and sign in with your wallet.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)
[Open bChat](https://www.bitcoinchat.online)

Building a BSV app? Let your users sign in with bWalletX: [bwalletx.com/connect](https://bwalletx.com/connect).

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Your $name is your token

In bWalletX, one name does three jobs: it's where people pay you, it's a token people can hold, and it's the key to your chat room.

handle@bwalletx.com→
$HANDLE→
$HANDLE room

## 1. Handles

Your handle is a paymail: an address that looks like an email, such as `yourname@bwalletx.com`. People send you money, tokens and messages to your name instead of a long string of letters and numbers. Claiming one is free.

A wallet has one main name. It can keep older names that still receive, and Settings › Identity lists every one of them, so nothing receives for you without you knowing. You can unlink any of them.

## 2. Sign in with X or Google

Prove who you are, and your name is verified:

### X → `yourhandle.x@bwalletx.com`

Sign in with X and you get your exact X username, marked as verified. Nobody else can claim it.

### Google → `yourname.gmail@bwalletx.com`

Sign in with a Gmail address and you get a matching verified name.

Your X or Google profile picture becomes your wallet's picture too. bWalletX never sees your X or Google password, and your keys never leave your device. If a wallet has a verified name, that name is its main name, token and room. Want a different identity? Add another account.

## 3. Tokenised handles

Turn your name into a token in one tap: $HANDLE for handle@bwalletx.com. It's a BSV-21 token on the Bitcoin SV blockchain, with a fixed supply that starts in your wallet. Its icon is your profile picture.

Anyone can copy a ticker, so bWalletX checks every token's signed creator record. Only the token actually made by that name's owner gets the check mark. Copycats don't.

Personal tokens are social tokens: they're for access and fun, not investments. They don't pay dividends.

## 4. The market

Every user token can be bought and sold on the bWalletX Exchange. List some of yours for sale at your own price, or buy someone else's to get into their room. Trades settle directly between wallets on chain; bWalletX never holds your tokens or money.

Before a token shows up in other wallets and the Exchange, its creator pays a one-off indexing deposit to the 1Sat indexer. It's a prepaid balance that pays for the token's transfers, not a fee to bWalletX.

## 5. Chat rooms

Every user token has a chat room. Hold the token, join the room. Inviting someone is as simple as sending them one token.

The room's owner sets its rules: how many tokens you need to hold to get in, and how chatting uses them up. For example, 1 token per character typed, burned or sent back to the owner. Every room can have its own economy.

## 6. Friends

The Friends tab in your wallet is your address book: people you've paid, called, chatted with or followed. A friend only needs a name; if they have a token, their row shows how many you hold, with a button to enter their room or buy in. Message, call or pay anyone in one tap.

[Get bWalletX for Android](https://bwalletx.com/android)
[Chrome extension](https://bwalletx.com/extension)
[All features](https://bwalletx.com/features)

bWalletX is in beta and some room rules are still being rolled out. Tokens can lose all value. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Sign in with Gmail

Make a bWalletX wallet with your Gmail account and it comes with a verified name. People pay you at it, hold it as a token and use it to get into your chat room.

you@gmail.com→
you.gmail@bwalletx.com→
$YOU.GMAIL

## How to do it

- [Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get) on your phone or computer.

- Tap Create account, then Continue with Google.

- Pick your Gmail account on Google's own sign-in page.

- Back in bWalletX, your name and picture are filled in. Choose a password and save your 12-word recovery phrase.

- Claim `yourname.gmail@bwalletx.com`. It's free.

Already have a wallet? Use Restore with your 12 words and Continue with Google to bring the same name back.

## Your name

Your name comes from your Gmail address. Dots don't count and anything after a `+` is ignored, the same way Gmail treats them.

jane.doe@gmail.com`janedoe.gmail@bwalletx.com`

janedoe+shop@gmail.com`janedoe.gmail@bwalletx.com`

jane_doe@googlemail.com`jane-doe.gmail@bwalletx.com`

Only `@gmail.com` and `@googlemail.com` addresses get a `.gmail` name, because only Google can prove who owns them. Work or school Google accounts can still sign in, then pick an ordinary name.

## What you get

### A verified paymail

People send you BSV, tokens and messages at `yourname.gmail@bwalletx.com`. It's marked verified, and nobody else can claim it.

### Your own token and room

Turn the name into $YOURNAME.GMAIL, a BSV-21 token with your Google picture as its icon. Hold the token, join your room.

### Your picture

Your Google profile picture becomes your wallet's picture, so friends recognise you in chats, calls and payments.

## What Google shares

bWalletX asks Google for three things only: your email address, your name and your profile picture. It never sees your Google password and can't read your email, contacts or files. Your wallet's keys are made on your device and never leave it; Google has nothing to do with them.

Signing in with Google proves the name. Your 12-word recovery phrase is still the only way to get your money back, so keep it safe.

[Social in bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/social)
[Privacy](https://bwalletx.com/privacy)

Sign in with Google and X are in bWalletX. The App Store and Google Play version, bWallet, doesn't have them yet. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Live. Your token is the ticket.

Creators go live in a room that only their token holders can enter. Hold the token and you’re in. The token, the payment and the room all sit in one wallet.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

## The idea

A creator’s room is gated by the creator’s token. Holders get in and watch the creator live: one person on camera, everyone else watching, with chat alongside. Anyone who doesn’t hold the token sees a “hold 1 to join” door, not the stream.

Think creator rooms and subscriber streams, except the subscription is a token you hold. You can keep it, sell it or give it away. Pay-per-minute and tips can sit on top, as options the creator chooses.

## Why in the wallet

bWalletX is a smart social super wallet: the things you do with your money belong in the place you keep it. Your token, your payment and the room are all in one app, so there’s no separate platform account, card or subscription to manage.

Holding a token to get in costs nothing extra. Payments go wallet to wallet; you pay the network fee, plus a small indexing fee when a token moves. Any fee on paid streams will be stated up front before you pay. The full version of rooms and spaces lives in [bChat](https://bwalletx.com/chat).

## How it works

- 1Your token. A creator has a token, such as a personal $NAME token (see [$handles](https://bwalletx.com/handles)).

- 2Your room. The room is set to “hold the token to enter”. The server checks holdings on every read and post, so selling the token closes the door.

- 3Go live. The creator opens a space and turns the camera on. Holders watch and chat; the creator can bring a viewer on stage.

- 4Optional extras. Pay-per-minute, tips, or burning a ticket to enter, as the creator chooses.

## What works today

- LiveToken rooms. Hold a token to enter a room. In bChat and in bWalletX.

- LiveSpaces in bChat. A host, speakers and listeners, a raise-hand queue, and opt-in camera for people on stage. Runs on our own video server.

- Live1:1 voice and video calls in bWalletX.

- ComingWatching a live room inside bWalletX. Today you go live and watch in bChat.

- ComingPay-per-minute watching. Paid a minute at a time, wallet to wallet, with a spending cap you set.

- ComingTips during a stream.

- ComingBigger audiences. Streams to more viewers than one video server can hold.

## Content rules

Creators are responsible for what they stream. They must follow the law where they and their viewers are, and our terms. Rooms and messages can be reported, and paid streams will need identity and age checks before they open.

## bWallet (App Store and Google Play) and bWalletX

- LiveBoth: 1:1 voice and video calls.

- LivebWalletX only: token rooms. They aren’t available in the store edition, so token-gated live rooms won’t be either.

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

Source: https://bwalletx.com/lounge

# bWallet Lounge

The Lounge is where bWallet and bWalletX people talk. Ask a question, share an idea, tell us what's broken. The team is in there too.

[Open the Lounge on bChat](https://www.bitcoinchat.online/room/LOUNGE)

## Already in your wallet

Every bWalletX and bWallet user is in the Lounge from day one. It's in your Chat tab, no invite and no token needed. Open Chat and you're there.

Don't want it? Leave any time, and it stays that way.

## What it is

It's a group chat room on bChat, ticker LOUNGE. Anyone can come in and read along. If you use bWalletX or bWallet you're already a member.

Stuck at 2am and nobody's around? Type `/b` followed by your question and the $b assistant answers, any time of day.

## How to join

- Open [bitcoinchat.online/room/LOUNGE](https://www.bitcoinchat.online/room/LOUNGE).

- Sign in with bWalletX, or with X or Google.

- Say hi.

# bWalletX Social

Social in bWalletX starts with your name. One name does three jobs: it's where people pay you, it's a token people can hold, and it's the key to your chat room. Around it: the Feed, calls, and a wallet that knows your friends.

handle@bwalletx.com→
$HANDLE→
$HANDLE room

## 1. Handles

Your handle is a paymail: an address that looks like an email, such as `yourname@bwalletx.com`. People send you money, tokens and messages to your name instead of a long string of letters and numbers. Claiming one is free.

A wallet has one main name. It can keep older names that still receive, and Settings › Identity lists every one of them, so nothing receives for you without you knowing. You can unlink any of them.

## 2. Sign in with X or Google

Prove who you are, and your name is verified:

### X → `yourhandle.x@bwalletx.com`

Sign in with X and you get your exact X username, marked as verified. Nobody else can claim it. [How X sign-in works](https://bwalletx.com/x).

### Google → `yourname.gmail@bwalletx.com`

Sign in with a Gmail address and you get a matching verified name. [How Gmail sign-in works](https://bwalletx.com/gmail).

Your X or Google profile picture becomes your wallet's picture too. bWalletX never sees your X or Google password, and your keys never leave your device. If a wallet has a verified name, that name is its main name, token and room. Want a different identity? Add another account.

## 3. Tokenised handles

Turn your name into a token in one tap: $HANDLE for handle@bwalletx.com. It's a BSV-21 token on the Bitcoin SV blockchain, with a fixed supply that starts in your wallet. Its icon is your profile picture.

Anyone can copy a ticker, so bWalletX checks every token's signed creator record. Only the token actually made by that name's owner gets the check mark. Copycats don't.

Personal tokens are social tokens: they're for access and fun, not investments. They don't pay dividends.

## 4. The market

Every user token can be bought and sold on the bWalletX Exchange. List some of yours for sale at your own price, or buy someone else's to get into their room. Trades settle directly between wallets on chain; bWalletX never holds your tokens or money.

Before a token shows up in other wallets and the Exchange, its creator pays a one-off indexing deposit to the 1Sat indexer. It's a prepaid balance that pays for the token's transfers, not a fee to bWalletX.

## 5. Chat rooms

Every user token has a chat room. Hold the token, join the room. Inviting someone is as simple as sending them one token.

The room's owner sets its rules: how many tokens you need to hold to get in, and how chatting uses them up. For example, 1 token per character typed, burned or sent back to the owner. Every room can have its own economy.

## 6. Social in your wallet

The Friends tab in your wallet is your address book, with your own $NAME token at the top: people you've paid, called, chatted with or followed. A friend only needs a name; if they have a token, their row shows how many you hold, with a button to enter their room or buy in. Message, call or pay anyone in one tap.

## 7. The Feed

Posts from BSV social apps (bChat, Twetch, Treechat and more) in one Feed: Following, For you and Latest. Post, reply, quote, like, tip the author in sats, or lock BSV behind a post (it stays yours and unlocks at the date shown). Bookmark, mute, block and report are built in.

## 8. Calls

Call anyone with a name, straight from the wallet. Calls are signed by your wallet key, so people know it’s really you; add the person to your friends from the call screen.

[Get bWalletX for Android](https://bwalletx.com/android)
[Chrome extension](https://bwalletx.com/extension)
[All features](https://bwalletx.com/features)

bWalletX is in beta and some room rules are still being rolled out. Tokens can lose all value. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

---

Source: https://bwalletx.com/x

# Sign in with X

Make a bWalletX wallet with your X account and it comes with a verified name: your X username. People pay you at it, hold it as a token and use it to get into your chat room.

@yourhandle→
yourhandle.x@bwalletx.com→
$YOURHANDLE

## How to do it

- [Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get) on your phone or computer.

- Tap Create account, then Continue with X.

- Sign in on X's own page and allow access.

- Back in bWalletX, your @handle and picture are filled in. Choose a password and save your 12-word recovery phrase.

- Claim `yourhandle.x@bwalletx.com`. It's free.

Already have a wallet? Go to Settings › Identity › Connect X or Google. The verified name becomes your wallet's main name, and your older name still receives.

Moving to a new phone? Use Restore with your 12 words and Continue with X to bring the same name back. If the 12 words belong to a different wallet, bWalletX says so and stops, so your name can't end up on the wrong wallet.

## Your name

Your name is your X username in lower case, with `.x` on the end. X allows underscores in usernames and paymail names don't, so an underscore becomes a hyphen.

@b0aseX`b0asex.x@bwalletx.com`

@Jane_Doe`jane-doe.x@bwalletx.com`

One X account gets one name, held by one wallet. If you change your X username later, the name you claimed stays as it was.

## What you get

### A verified paymail

People send you BSV, tokens and messages at `yourhandle.x@bwalletx.com`. It's marked verified, and nobody else can claim it, because only the owner of the X account can sign in as it.

### Your own token and room

Turn the name into $YOURHANDLE, a BSV-21 token with your X picture as its icon. Hold the token, join your room. In Exchange › Friends it's listed with your x.com link and a tick.

### Your picture

Your X profile picture becomes your wallet's picture, so friends recognise you in chats, calls and payments.

## How it differs from Gmail

It works the same way as [Sign in with Gmail](https://bwalletx.com/gmail), with two differences. X doesn't give us an email address, so your name comes from your username, not an address. And any X account can get a `.x` name, where only `@gmail.com` addresses get a `.gmail` one.

A wallet holds one verified name. If it already has a `.gmail` name, add another account for your `.x` one.

## What X shares

bWalletX reads three things from X: your username, your display name and your profile picture. It never sees your X password, can't post for you and doesn't read your messages. Your wallet's keys are made on your device and never leave it; X has nothing to do with them.

Signing in with X proves the name. Your 12-word recovery phrase is still the only way to get your money back, so keep it safe.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)
[Sign in with Gmail](https://bwalletx.com/gmail)
[Social in bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/social)
[Privacy](https://bwalletx.com/privacy)

Sign in with X and Google are in bWalletX (Android APK, Chrome extension, web and iPhone). The App Store and Google Play version, bWallet, doesn't have them yet. They aren't offered for agent accounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

Source: https://bwalletx.com/agent

# The b agent

The b agent is the AI assistant built into bWalletX. Tap the b in the centre of the top bar to chat with it: it knows how the wallet works, helps you design strategies, and in chat rooms you can call it in with `/b`.

### Looking for agent accounts: AIs with their own wallet?

Separate accounts that an AI runs for you, each with its own budget and its own ghost. [Agent accounts →](https://bwalletx.com/agents)

## Two ways to use it

### Your own key

Add an API key for Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter. It stays in secure storage on your device and requests go straight from your phone to that provider. We don't see them. This is the more private option.

### Pay per message

The wallet gets a quote, pays in BSV and gets the answer, with a daily limit. The price is set in US dollars and converted to sats at quote time.

## In chats: /b

Type `/b` followed by your question in a chat room and the b agent answers there, paid in $b.

## What it can do

Explain a feature
Create a strategy
Trade with a strategy
Buy or sell one

It has the wallet's usage guide as its system prompt, so it can explain features. In an agent account it can act, buying and sending, but only through the strategy rules the wallet enforces, never on its own judgement. [How strategies work →](https://bwalletx.com/strategies)

## Privacy and consent

Before the first message to each provider, a consent sheet shows what is sent (your message and the last 8 turns) and what isn't. You can revoke consent in Settings. The agent refuses input that looks like a recovery phrase or private key, and it has no long-term memory, by design.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)
[Agent accounts](https://bwalletx.com/agents)

The store builds use your own key only. The story so far: [009 The b agent: paid, or your own key](https://bwalletx.com/blog/009-the-b-agent). Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

Source: https://bwalletx.com/agents

# Agent accounts: every AI gets its own ghost

An agent account is a separate wallet account that an AI runs for you, with its own keys and its own budget. It trades, sends and reports inside the limits you set, and you can stop it or sweep everything back any time.

### Looking for the b agent?

The assistant you chat with inside the wallet is the b agent. [The b agent →](https://bwalletx.com/agent)

Traderrunning
Slow accumulator · cap $20/day
$120.00

Treasurerrunning
Tops up the other agents
$64.25

Reporterread only
Daily summary to chat
$0.00

Scoutstopped
$HANDLE fund · paused by you
$18.90

## The ghost is the agent's face

Make an account an agent account and it gets a pixel ghost in its own colour. It shows on the wallet card when that account is selected and is the account's avatar everywhere: the account menu, Settings and chat. One look tells you which agent you're in.

1st

2nd

3rd

4th

5th

6th

7th

8th

## What an agent account can do

### Spend only its budget

Its balance is all it can ever spend. Fund it from any of your accounts in one tap; your other accounts are never touched.

### Follow a strategy

Agree the rules in plain words, or load a strategy, and it trades by those rules and nothing else. [Strategies →](https://bwalletx.com/strategies)

### Show its work

An activity log lists every action, with links to the transactions. Add labels and an optional daily spending cap in dollars.

### Stop on your word

Stop one agent or Stop all agents. A stopped account refuses every spend until you resume it, and Sweep back moves every token, NFT and all the BSV home.

## Many agents

Run one AI per account, or one across several. A Trader on two strategy accounts, a Treasurer that tops them up, a Reporter that only reads: each sees only the accounts you give it.

## bAgents

bAgents is the home for agents on bWalletX: browse, set up and manage the AIs that run your agent accounts. [agents.bwalletx.com →](https://agents.bwalletx.com)

## Pair a computer, or Claude

The bWalletX CLI runs agent accounts on a laptop or a server. Pair it with your phone so the phone signs every request, or export an agent account's key file to run unattended. Every spend is checked first: the kill switch, the daily cap, at most 30 spends an hour, then the strategy's rules.

`# install (Node 20+)
npm i -g bwalletx
bwalletx login --account phone # scan the QR in your agent account
bwalletx agent run trader # run its strategy
bwalletx stop # kill switch
# Claude Code, over MCP
claude mcp add bwalletx -- npx -y bwalletx mcp`

Over MCP, Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any agent can manage the agent accounts you give it, within the same limits as the app. An AI can only load strategies on paper: going live is a step you take yourself. [CLI guide →](https://bwalletx.com/cli) · [MCP guide →](https://bwalletx.com/mcp)

## Start in a minute

In bWalletX, open the account menu and tap Add agent account, or go to Settings › Agents. Move in a small budget, give it a strategy, and its ghost appears on the card.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)
[Agents in the web wallet](https://web.bwalletx.com/agents)

Agent accounts spend real money: start with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# bWalletX CLI

Your wallet and your agents from the command line, on your laptop or a server.

npm i -g bwalletx→
bwalletx login→
bwalletx agent run

## Get started

``npm i -g bwalletx # Node 20+
bwalletx login --account phone # shows a QR: scan it in bWalletX from your agent account``

In bWalletX (5.1.40 or later), open your agent account, then Settings › Paired websites › Scan to connect. Check both screens show the same 4-digit code, choose what the CLI may do and for how long (1, 7 or 30 days), and tap Pair. Your keys never leave the phone.

For a server with no phone around, export a key file instead: Agents › your agent account › Run on a computer › Export for CLI, then `bwalletx key import ./trader.key.json`.

## Commands

``bwalletx accounts # paired and imported agent accounts
bwalletx balance --account trader # BSV and tokens, in dollars
bwalletx price <tokenId>
bwalletx send 1 name@bwalletx.com --account trader
bwalletx buy <tokenId> --max-usd 2 --account phone # cheapest listing, +1% fee, never over the cap
bwalletx strategy load ./slow-accumulator.json --account trader
bwalletx agent run trader # run its strategy unattended
bwalletx log --account trader
bwalletx stop # kill switch: refuse every spend``

## What works today (v0.2)

### Live

Balances, prices, the activity log, sending BSV to an address or paymail, and buying BSV-21 tokens from the Exchange. Strategies run by `agent run` trade for real once you load them live.

### Paired or key file

Paired (`bwalletx login`): the phone checks and signs every request, so bWalletX must be open on that agent account. Key file: runs unattended on a server.

### Coming

Selling, listing and minting from the CLI.

## Your keys stay safe

### Agent accounts only

Only agent accounts can be exported, never your main wallet. The key file is encrypted with a passphrase you choose and stays encrypted on disk.

### Limits

The agent account's balance is the budget. Every spend is checked first: the kill switch, the daily cap, at most 30 spends an hour, then the strategy's rules. Every action is logged.

Free example strategies and the file format: [Strategies](https://bwalletx.com/strategies) · [spec](https://bwalletx.com/strategies/spec). Source: [github.com/b0ase/bwalletx-cli](https://github.com/b0ase/bwalletx-cli) · [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bwalletx).

[Agent wallet](https://bwalletx.com/agent)
[Developers](https://bwalletx.com/developers)

Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)
